Status codes at a glance

The table below lists the status codes this deployment emits and the condition that produces each one.

CodeCondition
200The request was understood and the representation returned is the current state of the resource.
304The validator supplied by the client still matches, so the stored representation may be reused unchanged.
403The request was understood but the policy in force refuses it, and repeating the request will not help.
404No representation exists for the target, and the server does not say whether one ever did exist.
410A representation existed and has been removed deliberately, which is a stronger statement than 404.
429The client exceeded the rate the deployment is willing to serve, and the Retry-After field says when to return.

Operational checklist

  • Confirm that the conditional request path is exercised, because a deployment that never emits 304 is paying for every byte twice over.
  • Confirm that 403 is reported as received and never retried automatically, because retrying a policy refusal is how a client earns a block.
  • Confirm that 410 is preserved in the record, because collapsing it into 404 destroys the distinction the origin deliberately drew.
  • Confirm that Retry-After is honoured, because ignoring it converts a temporary limit into a permanent one for everyone sharing the address.
